uncited: *   **Input:** Four TT cores $C_1, C_2, C_3, C_4$ representing a 4D volume with spatial dimensions $N_1, N_2, N_3$ and time dimension $N_4$.
The TT ranks are $R_1, R_2, R_3, R_4$ (where $R_4=1$ for standard TT format).
*   **Output:** A reduced base tensor $T_c$ (pre-computation) and, for each requested time step $t$, a 3D spatial volume slice $V_t$ (runtime).
*   **TT Cores:** $C_k$ is a tensor of shape $R_{k-1} \times N_k \times R_k$ (with $R_0=R_4=1$).
*   **Reduced Base Tensor ($T_c$):** A 4D tensor of shape $N_1 \times N_2 \times N_3 \times R_3$.
Multiply the first three TT cores $C_1, C_2, C_3$ together to form the reduced base tensor $T_c$.
For a required time step $t$ (where $t \in [1, N_4]$), extract the $t$-th column vector $v_t$ from the last TT core $C_4$.
The shape of $v_t$ is $R_3 \times 1$ (effectively a vector of length $R_3$).
If $R_3$ is large, $T_c$ may become too large.
